cells.tense: You're here, with the first real piece in your hand.
cells.verb: putting the first concrete piece down
cells.place: where you set up how things will be organized
cells.ask: pick the next thing to start before anything makes you — one small, actual piece, chosen because you can see it's the one.
cells.core:
You're here, with the first real piece in your hand. Something concrete is ready to start, and you're the one setting the shape it will grow into — not controlling it, just giving it somewhere to stand. What you commit now is small, but it's the right small, and you're choosing it because you can see it, not because something is pushing.

That seeing is what's free to feed the next move: the next piece, chosen the same way.
cells.sheetLine: You're laying the first piece, and you chose it clearly.

cells.tense: You're already living in a version where the whole thing is built.
cells.verb: pinning down the first piece as if it has to be the last
cells.place: in how you set up what everything else will run on
cells.ask: before you fix another piece, say out loud what already feels whole here — and let what you know stay open enough to keep deepening. What comes back is a shape chosen from seeing, not from bracing.
cells.core:
You're already living in a version where the whole thing is built. So the first piece can't be a first piece; it has to hold the finished building, and every corner has to be fixed now before anything exists to fix. The frame is going up ahead of what it's for, and the committing has turned into bracing.

The way back isn't less starting. It's noticing what's already here and already felt, and letting that knowing keep moving instead of closing it.
cells.sheetLine: You're nailing down the frame before there's anything to frame.

cells.tense: The chance to start was back there, and you're still standing at it.
cells.verb: not putting the first concrete piece down
cells.place: where things are waiting to be organized into something workable
cells.ask: don't force yourself to start — instead, lay out plainly everything you actually see about this, nothing held back, no case made. Once it's all visible, the first piece tends to pick itself. What comes back is a beginning chosen from seeing, not from pressure.
cells.core:
The chance to start was back there, and you're still standing at it. Something was ready to be given a shape, and the first piece never got put down, so nothing has anything to stand on yet — the pieces stay loose, and you keep waiting for a surer version of the door you've already passed.

The missing thing isn't nerve. It's a full, honest look at what's actually there.
cells.sheetLine: You never put the first piece down, and everything's still loose.

cells.tense: You've already started, and you're calling it something that happened to you.
cells.place: in how you've already set up what everything runs on
cells.ask: take one piece you've been calling necessary, or obvious, or just how it fell out, and say plainly: I started that. What comes back is a shape you're choosing on purpose, not one you're pretending found you.
cells.core:
You've already started, and you're calling it something that happened to you. The first concrete piece is down, the shape things are taking is the one you gave them, and people are already arranging themselves around it — but you talk about it as circumstance, as what the situation required.

The starting is real and it's working. The claim on it is what's missing.
cells.sheetLine: You already set the shape. You keep saying it set itself.
